title: Kanban board
brief: Make the task board for our 'Website relaunch' project, sprint 14 (9 to 27 November). A white top bar holds the project name, the sprint dates and a 'New card' button. Below it, four equal columns: Backlog, In progress, Review and Done, each with a count of its cards in a small pill in the header. There are eleven cards in all. Each card has a coloured label (Design, Frontend, Content or Bug, each with its own colour), a short title, the assignee's initials in a round avatar and a due date. One card in progress is overdue and its date should be red; the cards in Done have their titles struck through and show when they were finished. It should feel light and organised, like a modern project tool, with an indigo accent.

requirements.text: Heading 'Website relaunch' with 'Sprint 14, 9 to 27 November' and a 'New card' button
Four columns in this order: Backlog, In progress, Review, Done
Each column header shows how many cards it holds: 3, 3, 2, 3 (eleven cards in all)
Every card shows a label, a title, an initials avatar and a date
Labels Design, Frontend, Content and Bug each have their own colour, used the same way on every card
Card titles and dates match the goal, e.g. 'Build the new pricing table' due Nov 18, 'Contact form validation' due Nov 16
'Menu closes on iOS scroll' is overdue: 'Due Nov 14' is shown in red
Done cards have struck-through titles and dates written 'Done Nov 10', 'Done Nov 11', 'Done Nov 12'
Columns are sections with headings and their cards are lists
Text, including labels and avatar initials, is easy to read against its background

designNotes: light and organised, soft grey columns
white cards with a faint shadow
indigo accent for the main button
